pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p1.text1: A captain who does not know where he is soon knows where the rocks are. Keep your chart, mark it well, and trust the lead more than your memory.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p2.list1_: Drag to pan, scroll to zoom.
Right-click to place a marker with a name: X marks the spot, an anchorage, a skull, a port or a danger. Click a marker to rename or remove it.
Your ship shows where you are and which way you head.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p2.text1: Every captain keeps a chart of his own, and it draws itself as you sail: the coasts within about 96 blocks are inked in as you pass, with hatched shallows, sandy beaches and the open sea, where the odd sea serpent lurks. Only the seas of the overworld are charted.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p2.text2: Craft a {item:pirates_n_ships:chart}**chart** from paper, leather and a feather, and use it to open your map. Or press **M** with the chart in either hand.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p3.text1: A {item:pirates_n_ships:map_tile}**map tile** (eight sticks around a paper) hangs on a wall or lies on a table. Set several side by side in a rectangle, all facing the same way, and they make one board, up to 8 tiles on a side.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p3.text2: **1.** Use any tile with your chart in hand: your chart opens with a frame the shape of the board.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p3.text3: **2.** Drag the frame over the waters you want, pick a zoom, and choose whether your markers go on it.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p3.text5: Drawing costs ink: an ink sac or glow ink sac for each tile. A single {item:pirates_n_ships:kraken_ink}**kraken ink** pays for eight.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p3.text6: Later, anyone who has charted more can use the board and press **Update**: what they know fills in the blank parchment, what was drawn before stays, and they pay only for the tiles that changed. **New** draws the board afresh at another place or zoom, and **Clear** wipes it; both ask you to click twice. Look at a tile to see who drew it, when, and where. Break a tile and it keeps its piece of the drawing; set it back and the board is whole again.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p4.list1_: **Two points off the starboard bow:** a little to the right of ahead.
**On the beam:** square off the side.
**Three points abaft the beam:** behind the beam, toward the stern.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p4.text1: The lookout in the crow's nest calls in points of the compass from the bow: 32 points to the circle, eight to each quarter.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p5.text1: Fences on pirate islands sell blank {item:pirates_n_ships:treasure_map}**treasure maps**, and wreck chests hold one now and then. Use a blank map and it marks the nearest buried treasure that no one has yet dug up; if there is none within reach, it stays blank.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p5.text2: While you hold the map it shows the island with a red X and tells you the way: "NW, 340 blocks". At the X, dig about two blocks into the sand and open the chest. Once the treasure is found, every map of it turns grey and keeps as a keepsake, and the next blank map leads somewhere new.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p5.text3: Every pirate island has a chest buried beneath two crossed logs. Dig at the cross.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p6.text1: The ocean floor is strewn with the bones of ships: a broken sloop, a field of scattered cargo, a mast stump with its yard, the stern of something larger. Each holds a chest of ship's stores: doubloons, rum, salted fish, rope, nails, lead shot, now and then a cutlass or a treasure map, rarely kraken ink.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p6.text2: Tall wrecks lie only in deep water; in the shallows you find cargo fields. Take something to let you breathe and see down there.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.title: Charts and navigation
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p1.text1: Sooner or later someone will want your ship, your cargo or your head. Learn the blade, the pistol and the great guns, and learn them before you need them.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p10.text1: Once your rope is made fast to a cleat or ring, look at it and use it: you hang from it and slide down to its lower end, riding along as both ships move. Sneak to let go. From your masthead down onto an enemy deck is the classic way across.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p10.text2: Or lay a {item:pirates_n_ships:boarding_plank}**boarding plank** (three wooden slabs over two iron nuggets). With the ships alongside, use it on the top of your gunwale facing the other ship. Up to six blocks of plank run out and come down on her deck; if her deck stands higher or lower, the plank climbs or falls on stepped ramps, two blocks at most. Keep the ships together: if her end slips more than a block and a half aside, the plank breaks and drops back to you. Sneak and use it with an empty hand to take it up again, from either end.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p10.text3: Hold the plank and look at your rail: the run it would lay shows in green before you commit, and a red cell shows what stands in the way.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p11.list1: Take goods from a merchant's hold while you stand aboard her, and you have plundered her.
Sink her, and the deed is yours if your shot was the last to strike her.
Kill every fighter aboard and hold her deck for a few seconds, and she is yours, crew and all.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p11.text1: Ships sail the sea lanes between the ports even when no one is watching, and when you come within sight of one she is there: a merchantman with goods in her hold and a few armed sailors, a navy patrol, or a pirate under the Jolly Roger. Navy and pirate sloops carry four guns, loaded, and a shot locker by the mast.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p11.text2: Taking a merchant is piracy in the navy's eyes. See [[pirates_n_ships:law|Law]].
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p12.list1: **Pirates,** in dark coats and bandanas, attack you and the navy on sight. They drop doubloons and now and then a cutlass.
**Navy soldiers,** in blue coats with white cross belts, carry muskets. They leave you be unless you are wanted; then they keep their distance, aim and fire. They drop lead shot and gunpowder.
**Navy officers,** in gold-trimmed coats, are deadly with the saber.
**Sailors** never fight; they run from danger.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p12.text1: Pirates and the navy fight each other wherever they meet. Striking or killing navy men is a crime; killing pirates is not.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p13.text1: Every pirate island has a captain, a named villain with a standing bounty of 300 doubloons on every notice board. He is a dangerous swordsman.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p13.text2: To fight him alone, sneak and use him with a sword in hand. If he accepts, his crew keeps out of the duel unless you strike them. The duel ends when one of you falls, when you run, or after five minutes. Strike him first and he refuses: there is no honour in it.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p13.text3: Slain, he drops his hat, maybe his coat, breeches and boots, a purse of doubloons, a treasure map of his island and your bounty proof. Taken alive in shackles, he pays better still. Five days after his fall a successor takes his place. Now and then he puts to sea in his own ship, and if you carry a letter of marque or a bounty proof, he hunts you.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p14.text1: Linger long at a navy outpost or a seafarer village and the pirates take notice. One day the cry goes up, "Sails on the horizon!", and the bells ring. Pirate sloops come in from the nearest island, drop anchor off the quay and put their fighters ashore. Kill them all and the raid is beaten off; either way the settlement is safe for five days afterward.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p15.list1: **Hats,** one point each: the {item:pirates_n_ships:pirate_hat}**pirate hat** (three black wool over leather, a bone and leather), the {item:pirates_n_ships:bandana}**bandana** (red wool, string, red wool), the {item:pirates_n_ships:navy_hat}**navy tricorn** (with white wool), the {item:pirates_n_ships:officer_hat}**officer's bicorne** (with a gold nugget), and the {item:pirates_n_ships:captains_hat}**captain's hat**, which you only win from a pirate captain.

**The captain's coat, breeches and boots,** in charcoal and gold, and **the officer's coat, breeches and boots,** in navy blue and white: three points for a coat, two for breeches, one for boots. All are crafted from wool, leather and a touch of gold.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p15.text1: Hats and coats are armour too.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p16.list1: Its eyes are its weak spots: they take triple harm.
Enough harm to a tentacle cuts it, and it lets go until it grows back.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p16.text1: The **kraken** lurks in the deep ocean and rises beside ships, more often at night and in storms. Its tentacles grip the hull and drag her down, beat masts to splinters and sweep the deck; swimmers are pulled under.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p16.text2: It leaves a {item:pirates_n_ships:kraken_beak}**kraken beak** and {item:pirates_n_ships:kraken_ink}**kraken ink**, prized by chart makers.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p17.text1: Sharks cruise every ocean a few blocks under the surface. A shark that spots you swimming circles before it charges and bites, and blood in the water drives it into a frenzy. Stay on deck or in a boat and it leaves you alone; climb out and it loses you at once.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p18.text1: In a thunderstorm at sea a **waterspout** may form: a turning column of spray with a low roar. Close to it you, your boat and loose things are pulled in and lifted, and the wind tears set sails down a step every few seconds. Steer clear, or furl first.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p18.text2: In the deep ocean, at any hour, a **whirlpool** may open: a slow ring of foam around a dark centre that draws everything inward. Near its heart it drags boats and swimmers under, and a ship caught there is turned about.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p2.list1_: {item:pirates_n_ships:rapier}**Rapier** (two iron ingots and a stick): light and long, made for the thrust.
{item:pirates_n_ships:cutlass}**Cutlass** (three iron ingots and a stick): heavy and wide, made for the slash.
{item:pirates_n_ships:saber}**Saber** (two iron ingots, a gold ingot and a stick): the officer's blade, good at both.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p2.list2_: **Slash:** a quick left click. A wide, short arc after a brief wind-up.
**Thrust:** hold left click a moment and release. Narrow, longer reach, harder, but slow to recover if it misses.

**Guard:** hold right click. It stops every blow from the front, but each blow costs stamina, the heavier the dearer. When you cannot pay, your guard breaks and you stagger. Blows from behind or the side ignore your guard.

**Parry:** a quick tap of right click just before a blow lands. The blow glances off, the attacker staggers, and for a second you may **riposte** for extra harm. A parry at nothing costs stamina and locks your parry for a moment.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p2.text1: Three blades are worth carrying, each with its own temper:
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p2.text2: With one of these in hand the mouse fights differently:
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p2.text3: Your stamina shows as a brass-framed bar while you hold a sword. Attacks, guarding and missed parries drain it; it refills when you rest. With an empty bar you can neither guard nor parry.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p2.text4: While you hold one of these swords, right click belongs to the blade. Put it away to open a door or take the helm.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p3.text1: Pirates fight with the same swordplay you do. Watch for the raised arm before a slash, or the arm drawn back before a thrust, and parry just before the blow. A pirate sometimes feints: he stops his swing to bait an early parry and strikes while your guard is spent. Navy officers are skilled duellists with the saber.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p4.text1: The {item:pirates_n_ships:pistol}**pistol** and the {item:pirates_n_ships:musket}**musket** (each two iron ingots, a flint and a plank) are single-shot flintlocks. The musket hits harder and flies flatter and truer; the pistol scatters.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p4.text2: **1.** **Load:** with {item:pirates_n_ships:lead_shot}**lead shot** (two iron nuggets make four) and gunpowder in your pack, hold right click: three seconds for the pistol, five for the musket. Let go early and nothing is lost.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p4.text3: **2.** **Aim:** with a loaded gun, hold right click. After a second of steady aim the shot is tighter, and the musket draws your eye in a little.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p4.text4: **3.** **Fire:** left click, while aiming or from the hip. From the hip the ball scatters wide.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p4.text5: Letting go of right click never fires; the gun stays loaded. Sneak to lower an aimed gun. A loaded gun shows a full gold bar in your hotbar and says "Loaded" in its tooltip.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p4.text6: In the rain a quarter of your shots misfire with a click; the charge stays in.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p5.show_m: Show me: loading and firing a cannon
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p5.text1: A {item:pirates_n_ships:cannon}**cannon** is cast from two iron ingots and a block of iron on a carriage of two logs and a plank. Click the deck block where the **front** of the carriage should stand: the rear takes the block toward you and the barrel overhangs one block ahead, so click the spot by the rail. Both halves need a block beneath them.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p5.text2: **1.** **Load:** use it with gunpowder, then with a {item:pirates_n_ships:cannonball}**cannonball** (four iron ingots make two). Powder first, always.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p5.text3: **2.** **Aim:** sneak and use it with an empty hand. The upper half of the block raises the barrel, the lower half lowers it, from 5° down to 20° up in steps of 5°.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p5.text4: **3.** **Fire:** use it with an empty hand.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p5.text5: The barrel needs five seconds to cool before fresh powder goes in. A ball hits hard and smashes the wooden block it strikes; a hole below a ship's waterline lets the sea in. A ball that grazes a hull at a shallow angle glances off; a square hit does the most harm. From a moving ship the shot carries her speed, and each shot pushes your ship back a little.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p5.text6: A cannon cannot turn sideways. Lay your ship so her broadside bears.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p6.list1_: {item:pirates_n_ships:chain_shot}**Chain shot** (two iron ingots and a chain make two): two balls on a chain. It flies slower and shorter than a ball, breaks no hull and rips through rigging. Through a square sail it tears the cloth, so the sail draws only with what is left; it cuts ropes and stays and breaks ratlines. Torn cloth mends by itself, a block a minute.

{item:pirates_n_ships:grapeshot}**Grapeshot** (eight iron nuggets in a string-tied bag make two): bursts from the muzzle as nine pellets in a narrow cone. Each pellet hurts whoever it hits and breaks nothing, and none strike your own deck. Fire it across a crowded enemy deck before you board.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p6.text1: Both load like a cannonball, after the powder.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p7.text1: The {item:pirates_n_ships:swivel_gun}**swivel gun** (three iron ingots over a stick) mounts on a fence, a wall, iron or brig bars, or any full block.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p7.text2: Load it with gunpowder, then a cannonball. Hold right click with an empty hand: the gun follows your eye while you hold, and fires when you let go. It hits less hard and less far than a cannon, breaks no planks and is ready again in three seconds. Sneak and use it to hear what it needs.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p8.text1: Post a hand at a gun with the whistle. Put gunpowder and shot in a chest, barrel or cargo crate within 4 blocks of the gun on the same ship, then blow **Load!**. On **Fire!** every manned, loaded gun goes off, and the crew reloads by itself from the supply, so a manned gun keeps firing as fast as it cools.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p8.text2: **Fire at will** lets the crews choose their own targets; see [[pirates_n_ships:crew|Crew]].
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p9.list1_: **Throw it:** right click. Its rope reaches 32 blocks.
**Shoot it:** put the hook in your off hand and a musket in your main hand. Hold use to load it into the musket (a full reload and a gunpowder), aim and fire. Its rope reaches 64 blocks.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p9.list2_: **Hooked into another ship from your own:** the rope hauls both ships together until they lie side by side.
**Haul by hand:** with the rope in hand, hold sneak and its length freezes. Walk back and it pulls the ship toward you.
**Climb:** right-click your own rope while it is in your hand and you go up it hand over hand, when the hook is at least two blocks above you.
**Make fast:** use a cleat or mooring ring of your own while your hook is out, and the rope is tied there.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p9.text1: The {item:pirates_n_ships:grappling_hook}**grappling hook** (three iron ingots and a string) bites into whatever it strikes: another ship, your own ship, or the land.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p9.text2: It slips off water, leaves and glass panes, and from creatures, and comes back after two seconds. Throwing a second hook frees the first. Sneak and use with an empty hand to let go. The rope parts if it is stretched past its length.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.title: Weapons and combat
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p1.heading: Crew
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p1.text1: One captain cannot work the winch, the helm, the pumps and the guns at once. A crew can. Hire good hands, feed them, pay them and give them a dry place to sleep, and they will sail your ship for you.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p10.heading: Wages and desertion
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p10.text1: Every dawn each hand wants 2 doubloons. The pay comes from the chests, barrels and cargo crates aboard, the ones nearest the helm first, and the lowest in spirits are paid first. If the coin aboard runs short, the rest comes out of your own purse while you are at sea in that world.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p10.text2: A hand whose morale stays below 20 for two dawns means to desert. He tells you so and walks off at the next port the ship comes within 48 blocks of, or wherever she is after three more dawns. Feed him, pay him and lift his spirits above 20 again, and he changes his mind.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p10.text3: On some seas a whole crew that stays miserable for three dawns rises in mutiny, turns pirate and takes the ship from you. Your server tells you whether yours is such a sea.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p11.heading: Fire at will
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p11.list1_1: Under the navy flag: the Jolly Roger, and ships whose false colours are found out.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p11.list1_2: Under the Jolly Roger: navy ships, merchants and unflagged ships.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p11.list1_3: Under a merchant flag or none: only the Jolly Roger.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p11.text1: Order **Fire at will** and your gun crews take over their cannons. Each crew lays its gun on the nearest hostile ship within its arc and 64 blocks, leads a moving target, loads from the powder and shot nearby and fires when the shot will tell.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p11.text2: Who is hostile depends on your own flag:
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p11.text3: Nobody fires on a ship that has struck her colours, and your crew holds fire if you strike yours. A cannon cannot turn sideways, so turn the ship to bring the guns to bear. **Release crew** ends it. The guns themselves are in [[pirates_n_ships:combat|Weapons and combat]].
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p2.heading: Hiring hands
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p2.list1_1: A sailor asks 10 doubloons, a navy rating 15, a pirate 20.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p2.list1_2: Villagers will not sign on with a captain they refuse to trade with.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p2.list1_3: Pirates sign on only with a friend of the pirates or a captain of some infamy, a Buccaneer or worse.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p2.list1_4: Navy ratings sign on only with an enlisted officer.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p2.text1: Every harbour master's desk has a **Crew** tab. Each day a port has a few souls looking for a berth: sailors at seafarer villages, pirates at pirate islands, navy ratings at navy outposts. Each asks a one-time fee and then a daily wage.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p2.text2: Before you hire, bring your own ship in and lie within about 32 blocks of the port. The new hand walks straight aboard and waits on deck.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p2.text3: Every hand needs a free {item:pirates_n_ships:hammock}**hammock**. Hang more hammocks before you take on more crew; the desk refuses a hand you cannot bunk.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p3.heading: Stations
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p3.text1: A station is a block a hand can work: the {item:pirates_n_ships:sail_winch}**sail winch**, the **helm**, the {item:pirates_n_ships:capstan}**capstan**, the {item:pirates_n_ships:bilge_pump}**bilge pump**, the {item:pirates_n_ships:cannon}**cannon**, the {item:pirates_n_ships:swivel_gun}**swivel gun** and the {item:pirates_n_ships:crows_nest}**crow's nest**.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p3.text2: A hand at a station stays at his post while the ship sails and turns. He walks there across the deck, even under way, and the station starts its work only when he has arrived. If he cannot reach it, or has not got there after ten seconds, he is put there anyway.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p3.text3: A hand leaves his station when it is broken, when the ship is taken apart, or when he dies.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p4.heading: The captain's whistle
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p4.list1_1: Use it on a hand, then on a station: he takes that station and stays there.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p4.list1_2: Use it on a hand at a station: he is released.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p4.list1_3: Sneak and use it on a hand to dismiss him from your service. Only you, or whoever hired him, may do so.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p4.list1_4: Use it in the air to open the order wheel. Point at an order and click, or hold the use key, aim and let go. Escape closes the wheel.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p4.text1: The {item:pirates_n_ships:captains_whistle}**captain's whistle** is how a captain speaks to his crew.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p4.text2: The orders on the wheel: **Hoist sails**, **Reef sails**, **Furl sails**, **Man the pumps**, **Fire!**, **Load!**, **Fire at will**, **Drop anchor**, **Weigh anchor** and **Release crew**.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p4.text3: No whistle in your sea chest? The ship screen at the helm gives every one of these orders too, and assigns, releases and dismisses hands. See [[pirates_n_ships:ships|Ships]].
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p5.heading: Orders, not assignments
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p5.text1: You need not post every hand yourself. Blow an order and every unmanned station that can carry it out becomes an open job. Free hands on deck take the nearest one by themselves within a second, get to work and stay there afterwards. A hand you posted yourself stays put and is never moved.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p5.text2: A hand gets to work without a word; he only speaks up when he cannot do it ("This ship has no sails, captain!"). Each step of trim takes him two seconds; the sails change when the work is done.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p5.text3: If nobody can carry an order out, you are told why: no ship under you, no station aboard that takes it, nothing to do, or what is wrong with the rig. If every hand is busy you hear "No free hands", and the job waits for the next hand who comes aboard.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p5.text4: **Release crew** sends every hand off his station, ends **Fire at will** and cancels the open jobs.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p6.heading: A helmsman
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p6.text1: Post a hand at the helm and he keeps her steady. He turns the wheel toward the course he is given and puts the rudder midships when he arrives ("We've arrived, captain!"). He does not touch the sails: order **Hoist sails** as well.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p6.text2: Take the wheel yourself at any time and he lets go; release it and he steers on. If the ship stops making headway with her sails set, he tells you she is stuck.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p7.heading: Meals
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p7.text1: Twice a day, at noon and at sunset, the hands who are off duty sit down by the {item:pirates_n_ships:pantry}**pantry** (or the water barrel) and eat for a few seconds. An order gets them up at once.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p7.text2: The meal is a sight to see, nothing more: the crew's rations are taken once a day, at dawn. What they eat and drink, and what happens when the pantry runs dry, is in [[pirates_n_ships:provisions|Provisions]].
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p8.heading: Hammocks and rest
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p8.text1: Hang a {item:pirates_n_ships:hammock}**hammock** between two supports at the same height, such as fence posts, walls, logs or the hull side: click the block next to one support while looking toward the other.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p8.text2: At nightfall every hand who is not at a station turns in to the nearest free hammock and gets up at dawn. A night in a hammock lifts his morale; a night aboard without a free hammock lowers it, and he will grumble. Hands on watch all night are not affected, and an order at night gets sleepers up at once. Each hammock is one bunk.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p8.text3: You may sleep in one too, on land or aboard: right-click a free one at night and you lie in it as in a bed. Aboard you stay in it while she sails, you count toward skipping the night, and the dawn puts you on your feet beside it. Sleeping there sets your respawn point, and aboard that point sails with the ship.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p8.text4: The captain sleeps in a {item:pirates_n_ships:sea_cot}**sea cot**, a wooden bed for the great cabin, which works the same way at sea.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p9.heading: Morale
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p9.list1_1: A night in a hammock: a little up. A night without one: down by ten.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p9.list1_2: Paid on time: up by one. Unpaid: down by eight.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p9.list1_3: Hungry: down by ten a day. Thirsty: down by twenty-five a day.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p9.list1_4: A ration of rum: up a little each day.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p9.list1_5: Scurvy: down every day until it is cured.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p9.text1: Every hand has a morale between 0 and 100; a new hand comes aboard at 70. You read it on the ship screen, or by using the whistle on him.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p9.text2: Hungry hands work at three quarters of their speed, thirsty hands at half.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.title: Crew
pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.p1.te: Every captain starts the same way: with planks, a helm and more courage than sense. Follow these steps in order and you will be under sail before the sun is down.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.p10.t: A shipwright will build you a sloop. At a seafarer village, open the harbour master's desk and look at the **Orders** tab. Pay in doubloons, bring the logs and wool he asks for, and come back for her when she is ready. [[pirates_n_ships:ships|Ships]] tells you more.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.p2.sh: Show me: building and assembling a ship
pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.p2.te: Build a hull of wood floating in the water. Planks, slabs, stairs and glass keep the sea out; a hollow hull with a deck floats high and dry.
Leave a gap of one block to the shore, the quay or any other build. Everything that touches the hull becomes part of the ship.

Natural ground never goes to sea: dirt, sand, raw stone, ore, gravel, ice and leaves stay behind when the ship is launched. Cut and crafted blocks (cobblestone, bricks, logs and planks) sail with her.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.p3.te: Craft a {item:pirates_n_ships:helm}**helm** from four sticks and a plank and place it on the deck. Stand behind it and look the way she should sail: the bow is where the helmsman looks.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.p4.te: Raise a mast of logs or fences. Across it set two rows of {item:pirates_n_ships:yard}**yards**, the lower one 2 to 8 blocks below the upper. Then place a {item:pirates_n_ships:sail_winch}**sail winch** anywhere on deck.
Add a {item:pirates_n_ships:capstan}**capstan** if you want an anchor, and you will.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.p5.te: Use the helm. Every block joined to it becomes one ship: she floats, rolls with the sea, and keeps her hold dry.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.p6.te: Use the sail winch: furled, then half, then full. The wind fills the canvas and she gathers way.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.p7.te: Hold right-click on the helm to take the wheel. Move the mouse, or hold A and D: right or D turns her to starboard, left or A to port. The line above your hotbar shows the rudder. Let go and the wheel stays where you left it.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.p8.te: Use the capstan to let go the anchor, and again to weigh it.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.p9.te: Sneak and use the helm with an empty hand to open the ship screen, then press **Disassemble** twice. She must lie nearly still and level first.
That is the whole of it. Now read [[pirates_n_ships:ships|Ships]] to learn what keeps her afloat, and [[pirates_n_ships:sailing|Sailing]] to learn how to make her go where you want.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.title: Your first ship
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p1.heading: Flags
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p1.text1: A flag is a promise. It tells every ship on the horizon who you are and what you mean to do, and the sea holds you to it. Choose your colours with care, and know what it costs to lie with them.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p2.heading: The colours
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p2.list1_1: {item:pirates_n_ships:merchant_flag}**Merchant flag** (a stick, two white wool, red dye), or no flag at all: neutral to everyone.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p2.list1_2: {item:pirates_n_ships:navy_flag}**Navy flag** (a stick, two blue wool, white dye): the navy and the merchants are friends, the pirates foes.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p2.list1_3: {item:pirates_n_ships:jolly_roger_flag}**Jolly Roger** (a stick, two black wool, a bone): the pirates are friends, the navy hunts you, and merchants may strike to you.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p2.list1_4: **Any banner:** your own flag, neutral to all. The cloth shows the banner's colour and every one of its patterns.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p3.heading: The flagpole
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p3.list1_1: **Use it with a flag:** the flag runs up the pole and flies after three seconds; you get the old one back.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p3.list1_2: **Use it with an empty hand:** strike the colours (the flag comes down but stays on the pole), or raise them again.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p3.list1_3: **Sneak and use it with an empty hand:** take the flag down into your hand.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p3.text1: A {item:pirates_n_ships:flagpole}**flagpole** is three sticks stood on end; it makes two. The flag hangs downwind from its top, a block high and a block and a half long, so leave it room.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p3.text2: Stack flagpoles to raise one tall pole, up to 6 blocks. The top flies the flag, and you may work it from any block of the pole. Placing a pole on top takes the flag up with it; breaking one in the middle splits it in two, and the upper part keeps the flag.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p4.heading: What your flag tells the law
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p4.list1_1: **Under the Jolly Roger** the navy fires on everyone aboard on sight, and being seen under it is a crime. Pirates let you be.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p4.list1_2: **Under the navy flag** you pass the navy, as long as your record is clean and the navy thinks well of you. A suspect who flies it may be found out by any navy soldier in sight. Then you are charged heavily, and the navy hunts your ship for five minutes whatever she flies.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p4.list1_3: A navy ship with a manned crow's nest sees your flag half again as far and sees through it half again as fast.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p4.text1: A ship flies the highest flag on her poles.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p4.text2: Firing on a ship that has struck her colours, or on one under a merchant flag or a banner, is a crime. If your crew fires, the charge is yours as her owner.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p5.heading: Striking your colours
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p5.text1: Strike your flag and you surrender: the navy and the pirates stop attacking. A navy patrol that sees you strike holds its fire, keeps you in sight for half a minute and sails on. Raise the Jolly Roger again and the chase is back on. The [[pirates_n_ships:law|Law]] chapter tells you what your crimes cost.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p6.heading: Banners and dyed sails
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p6.list1_1: Use a **dye** on the upper yard of a square sail, or the head cleat of a triangular one: the whole cloth takes the colour, and one dye is spent. White dye brings back the plain canvas.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p6.list1_2: A large square sail can carry a **banner**: use the banner on its upper yard. The cloth takes the banner's colour with its patterns drawn upright over it. Both yards must be at least 3 blocks long and 2 blocks apart.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p6.list1_3: Sneak and use the yard with an empty hand to take the banner back; breaking the yard block that holds it drops it. While a banner hangs, dyes are refused. Triangular sails take dye only.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p6.text1: Hoist any banner on a flagpole to fly your own flag: the cloth takes the banner's colour and patterns, its top edge at the pole.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p6.text2: Your canvas can carry colour too.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p6.text3: Colours are only for show: they never change what a sail does, and they stay through launching, taking apart and every change of trim.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.title: Flags
pirates_n_ships.almanac.inventory.p1.tex: Every block and item a sea-going hand may need, with a line on each and the chapter that tells the rest.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.inventory.p2.lis: {item:pirates_n_ships:helm}**Helm:** launches, steers and takes apart a ship. [[pirates_n_ships:ships|Ships]]
{item:pirates_n_ships:ships_bell}**Ship's bell:** rings when struck.
{item:pirates_n_ships:bilge_pump}**Bilge pump:** pumps a flooded hold. A station.
{item:pirates_n_ships:hull_patch}**Hull patch:** closes a breach.
{item:pirates_n_ships:flagpole}**Flagpole:** flies your colours. [[pirates_n_ships:flags|Flags]]
{item:pirates_n_ships:flag_pedestal}**Flag pedestal:** a carved plinth a flagpole stands in.
{item:pirates_n_ships:nameplate}**Nameplate:** shows her name.

{item:pirates_n_ships:figurehead_mermaid}{item:pirates_n_ships:figurehead_lion}{item:pirates_n_ships:figurehead_eagle}{item:pirates_n_ships:figurehead_skull}**Figureheads:** a mermaid, lion, eagle or skull for the bow.
{item:pirates_n_ships:ship_lantern}**Ship's lantern:** a lantern that burns under water.
{item:pirates_n_ships:stern_window}**Stern window:** shuttered windows for the great cabin.
{item:pirates_n_ships:rope_coil}**Rope coil:** coiled rope for the deck.
{item:pirates_n_ships:yard}**Yard:** a spar; two on a mast make a square sail. [[pirates_n_ships:sailing|Sailing]]
{item:pirates_n_ships:chart_table}**Chart table:** a captain's table.
{item:pirates_n_ships:sea_cot}**Sea cot:** the captain's bed at sea.
{item:pirates_n_ships:hammock}**Hammock:** a bunk for one hand. [[pirates_n_ships:crew|Crew]]
{item:pirates_n_ships:boarding_plank}**Boarding plank:** a bridge to an enemy deck.

{item:pirates_n_ships:oak_railing}{item:pirates_n_ships:oak_railing_port}**Railing, railing port:** a rail along the edge of a block, with posts where the run ends or turns; click again to rail another edge. The port is the opening: a cannon fires through it, a boarding plank goes out over its sill, and a swivel gun or ratlines sit on a railing.
{item:pirates_n_ships:cleat}**Cleat:** holds a stay, a rope line or a grappling rope.
{item:pirates_n_ships:rope}**Rope:** three string; rigs stays and rope lines.
{item:pirates_n_ships:sail_winch}**Sail winch:** works every sail aboard. A station.
{item:pirates_n_ships:capstan}**Capstan:** drops and weighs the anchor. A station.
{item:pirates_n_ships:mooring_ring}**Mooring ring:** catches and holds a grappling hook.
{item:pirates_n_ships:ratlines}**Ratlines:** rope nets for climbing aloft.
{item:pirates_n_ships:crows_nest}**Crow's nest:** the lookout's barrel. A station.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.inventory.p3.lis: {item:pirates_n_ships:cargo_crate}**Cargo crate:** 32 stacks of one item. [[pirates_n_ships:trade|Cargo and trade]]
{item:pirates_n_ships:hardtack}**Hardtack,** {item:pirates_n_ships:salted_fish}**salted fish,** {item:pirates_n_ships:salt_pork}**salt pork:** food that never spoils.
{item:pirates_n_ships:rum}**Rum:** cheers a crew and warms a swimmer.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.inventory.p4.lis: {item:pirates_n_ships:lead_shot}**Lead shot:** a ball for pistol or musket.
{item:pirates_n_ships:swivel_gun}**Swivel gun:** a small gun on a yoke. A station.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.inventory.p5.lis: {item:pirates_n_ships:bounty_proof}**Bounty proof:** proof of a kill; hand it to a navy officer.
{item:pirates_n_ships:ship_commission}**Ship commission:** an armed sloop earned by rank.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.inventory.p6.lis: {item:pirates_n_ships:map_tile}**Map tile:** a board for a drawn chart.

{item:pirates_n_ships:shipwright_toolkit}**Shipwright's toolkit,** from the {item:pirates_n_ships:carpenters_hammer}**carpenter's hammer,** {item:pirates_n_ships:saw}**saw** and {item:pirates_n_ships:nails}**nails:** joins a broken ship.
{item:pirates_n_ships:kraken_beak}**Kraken beak,** {item:pirates_n_ships:kraken_ink}**kraken ink:** spoils of the deep.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.inventory.p7.tex: Every one of them is in the "Pirates 'n' Ships" tab of the creative inventory, with spawn eggs for the folk and beasts of the sea.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.inventory.title: The ship's inventory
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p1.heading: Law
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p1.text1: The Crown keeps a ledger on every soul at sea, and on every beast that bites. Steal, strike or sail under false colours and your name goes in it. Stay honest and the navy is your friend; turn pirate and you had better be fast.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p10.heading: Navy patrols
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p10.text1: The navy sends patrols between its outposts and out toward the pirate islands. A patrol keeps a lookout of some 256 blocks and gives chase to any ship under the Jolly Roger, any whose false colours it has seen through, and any whose captain is wanted or carries a bounty of 50 doubloons or more.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p10.text2: It circles you at about 20 blocks while its guns fire. Strike your colours and it falls silent. Outrun it and it gives up the chase.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p11.heading: Careers
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p11.list1_1: **The navy.** Talk to a navy officer with an empty hand and enlist once the navy trusts you: a good name with it, no bounty and no friends among the pirates. Pirates killed, prisoners brought in, navy quests and a growing name promote you: Midshipman, Lieutenant, Captain, Commodore, Admiral. Firing on the navy or a merchant in service is desertion.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p11.list1_2: **Infamy.** Plunder fenced, ships taken and a name among the pirates make you a Buccaneer, a Dread Captain and at last a Pirate Lord. A known pirate is never taken into the navy.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p11.list1_3: **Letter of marque.** Not ready to serve? Buy one from a navy officer for 200 doubloons once the navy thinks well of you. Every pirate you kill under it earns prize money.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p11.text1: There are two ladders, and you may climb only one.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p11.text2: Rank has its rewards. A Lieutenant flies the navy flag by right, docks free at navy outposts and receives the officer's bicorne, a saber and the officer's coat, breeches and boots. A navy Captain receives a {item:pirates_n_ships:ship_commission}**ship commission** for an armed navy sloop; a Dread Captain is granted a pirate sloop at a pirate island's fence. A navy Captain may also order any ship at a navy outpost's desk for less than the villages ask.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p11.text3: Your title rides before your name in chat and over your head, and before your ship's name when you name her.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p2.heading: Your record
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p2.list1_1: Theft from a village chest, or striking a villager: 5.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p2.list1_2: Striking the navy, or being seen under the Jolly Roger: 10.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p2.list1_3: Attacking a neutral ship, press-ganging a prisoner, or being caught with plunder aboard: 15.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p2.list1_4: Offering stolen goods at a village or navy desk: 17.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p2.list1_5: Killing a villager: 20. Killing a navy man: 30.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p2.list1_6: Caught under false colours, or firing on a ship that struck: 40.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p2.list1_7: Piracy (taking a ship): 50. Deserting the navy: 60.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p2.text1: Every crime adds to your record:
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p2.text2: From 10 you are a **suspect**, from 50 **wanted**, and from 200 **notorious**. Five minutes after your last crime your record begins to fade, by 10 a day.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p2.text3: Theft counts only when someone sees it: a villager, a trader or a navy man nearby. Putting things into a chest is no crime.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p3.heading: Fines
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p3.text1: Hold doubloons and right-click a navy officer to pay your fine: 3 doubloons a point, as many whole points as you can afford. He will not deal with a wanted man, and no coin buys a pardon for the notorious.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p4.heading: Bounties
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p4.text1: At a record of 50 the navy puts a price on your head of twice your record. It grows as your record grows and is withdrawn once the record falls below 25.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p4.text2: Kill someone with a price on their head and a {item:pirates_n_ships:bounty_proof}**bounty proof** lands in your pack. Right-click a navy officer with it to collect. Bring the quarry in alive and it pays half again as much. A claim wipes the quarry's record clean.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p5.heading: The notice board
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p5.text1: The {item:pirates_n_ships:notice_board}**notice board** (planks and paper) lists every bounty: who is wanted, for how much, who placed it and when, and whether there is one on you.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p5.text2: To place a bounty of your own, type a name, enter at least 10 doubloons and press **Place**. The coin comes out of your pack.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p6.heading: Shackles and prisoners
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p6.list1_1: Use them on a creature at a quarter of its health or less: it becomes your prisoner. It stops fighting and never wanders off. Bosses cannot be taken, and players only where the server allows it and they carry a bounty.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p6.list1_2: Use them on your prisoner to lead it, or to let go. A led prisoner follows like a beast on a lead.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p6.list1_3: A prisoner left alone outside a cell tries to slip away.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p6.text1: {item:pirates_n_ships:shackles}**Shackles** (two iron ingots and a chain) take a beaten foe alive.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p7.heading: Turning in prisoners
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p7.list1_1: A prisoner with a bounty pays half again the bounty; a pirate earns a reward besides.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p7.list1_2: A shackled navy man or merchant can be ransomed back the same way.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p7.text1: Walk up to a navy officer with your prisoners close by and right-click him with an empty hand.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p7.text2: Hold the {item:pirates_n_ships:captains_whistle}**captain's whistle** and right-click a shackled sailor on your own ship to press-gang him into your crew. He comes aboard sullen, and it is a crime. Sneak and right-click your own prisoner with an empty hand to set him free.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p8.heading: The brig
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p8.text1: {item:pirates_n_ships:brig_bars}**Brig bars** connect like iron bars. The {item:pirates_n_ships:brig_door}**brig door** locks with a {item:pirates_n_ships:brig_key}**brig key** (an iron ingot over an iron nugget): use the key on the door to lock it, and again to unlock it.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p8.text2: Any key opens any brig door. Keep your keys away from your prisoners.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p8.text3: A locked door opens only for the one who placed it, and ignores redstone. A prisoner standing in a closed space of at most 64 blocks, walled by solid blocks, bars and a locked brig door, is **in a cell** and does not try to escape, unless your crew's spirits sink so low that the watch grows careless.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p9.heading: The three powers
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p9.list1_1: Killing pirates pleases the navy. Killing navy men, plundering merchants and selling to fences wins the pirates over. Trading at villages pleases the villagers.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p9.list1_2: Good standing gets you better prices; bad standing worse. Villagers stop trading with you at −60.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p9.list1_3: Pirates leave you be once they like you well enough, until you strike first. Fall to −60 with the navy and it fires on sight.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p9.text1: The sea has three powers: the navy, the pirates and the merchants. Their quarrels rise and cool with every deed done at sea, and when the navy and the pirates are at each other's throats there are more patrols, more hunting and more raids.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p9.text2: Each power remembers you, from −100 to 100: the navy, the pirates and the villagers.

pirates_n_ships.almanac.ledger.p1.text1: These pages are for the keeper of a server, not for the hand at the wheel. Here are the settings that change how the sea plays, and the orders an operator may give. Every feature has a switch and every strength a value; only the ones a keeper reaches for first are written here.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ledger.p10.text1: Ship templates, trade goods and weapon timings are data files under data/<namespace>/pirates\_n\_ships/, and block and item tags decide what never sails (terrain, never\_assemble), what keeps water out (watertight, not\_watertight), which foods keep or cure scurvy, and what may be hoisted (flags). A datapack can replace any of them, or add to the Almanac itself: see the mod's chapter format.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ledger.p2.text1: Open them in game under Mods, then Pirates 'n' Ships, then Config (on a Fabric server with Mod Menu installed). Gameplay settings sit in the server config, which every client receives; how things look and sound sits in each player's client config.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ledger.p2.text2: Settings are written as section.name, with the default after the colon.
